facts.statement: Polesinesuchus aurelioi is the fifth aetosaur species discovered in South America.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Polesinesuchus aurelioi, the fifth aetosaur species known from South America to date.

facts.statement: The genus Polesinesuchus was named in 2014 by a team of seven researchers including Lúcio Roberto-da-Silva.
facts.quote: Polesinesuchus was first named by Lúcio Roberto-da-Silva, Julia B. Desojo, Sérgio F. Cabreira, Alex S. S. Aires, Rodrigo T. Müller, Cristian P. Pacheco and Sérgio Dias-da-Silva in 2014

facts.statement: The only known fossil material of Polesinesuchus is a single partially articulated partial skeleton.
facts.quote: It is known solely from its holotype specimen, a partially articulated partial skeleton.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Polesinesuchus was collected from the Santa Maria Formation dating to the late Carnian and earliest Norian stages.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Santa Maria Formation which dates back to the late Carnian and earliest Norian stages of the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: The known specimen of Polesinesuchus is estimated to be 76 cm long and likely a two-year-old juvenile.
facts.quote: Polesinesuchus is known from a relatively small-sized individual with an estimated length of 76 cm, probably a two-year-old juvenile based on the incomplete fusion of neural arches to their centra in the whole vertebral column.

facts.statement: Polesinesuchus was originally distinguished from other aetosaurs by a unique combination of vertebral characters thought to be independent of growth stage.
facts.quote: Polesinesuchus can be distinguished from all other aetosaurs by a unique combination of characters not controlled by ontogeny, most of which are found in its vertebrae.

facts.statement: Polesinesuchus lacks hyposphene articulations in its cervical and mid-dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: In Polesinesuchus, hyposphene articulations are absent in both cervical and mid-dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: In 2021, researchers found that many features distinguishing Polesinesuchus actually fall within the variation seen in juvenile Aetosauroides.
facts.quote: Yet, in 2021, it was found that many of these features fall within the range of variation present in juvenile specimens of Aetosauroides.

facts.statement: Due to similarities with juvenile Aetosauroides, Polesinesuchus has been suggested as a junior synonym of that genus.
facts.quote: For these reasons, Polesinesuchus was suggested as a junior synonym of Aetosauroides.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis recovered Polesinesuchus as the sister taxon of Aetobarbakinoides.
facts.quote: Polesinesuchus was recovered as the sister taxon of Aetobarbakinoides, known from the same geological formation.

facts.statement: Close relatives of the Polesinesuchus clade include the South American genera Aetosauroides and Neoaetosauroides.
facts.quote: Close relatives of this clade included Aetosauroides and Neoaetosauroides, both of which are also from South America.

facts.statement: Polesinesuchus is an extinct stagonolepidid aetosaur from the Late Triassic of southern Brazil.
facts.quote: Polesinesuchus is an extinct genus of stagonolepidid aetosaur known from the Late Triassic of southern Brazil.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Polesinesuchus, including skull and postcranial parts of a juvenile, were found in the Santa Maria Supersequence of the late Carnian and early Norian.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles, partes del cráneo y del esqueleto postcraneal de un individuo juvenil, se han hallado en la Supersecuencia Santa Maria de finales del Carniense y principios del Noriense.

facts.statement: Polesinesuchus lived during the Carnian stage, approximately 237 to 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)
